claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: On Local Services Ads, Google records all inbound customer calls that come through the Google forwarding number in the US and Canada.
claims.quote: Note that in the US and Canada, all inbound calls from customers via the Google forwarding number are recorded by Google to improve quality and support policies and research

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: On Local Services Ads calls, the customer is told by a pre-recorded message before the business hears the "Call from Google" prompt.
claims.quote: customers are notified of this by a pre-recorded message immediately before you hear the

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: Google's general Local Services help says phone calls and other communications delivered through Google may be monitored or recorded.
claims.quote: All phone calls, emails, and text-based communications delivered through Google may be monitored or recorded to improve quality and support policies and research
claims.note: General statement; the page does not limit it to a country in this sentence. The specific US/Canada recording rule is the previous claim.

claims.question: Q1
claims.claim: Google's Google Ads help says it monitors and records a small percentage of calls started from call-only ads or call assets, for some US advertisers.
claims.quote: Google monitors and records a small percentage of phone calls that are initiated by a call-only ad or call asset for some advertisers in the United States
claims.note: This older 'About call recording' page names only the US; the current recording page (see Q2 claims) names US and Canada.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Google's current Google Ads help page says call recording is now turned on by default to allow AI-powered lead qualification.
claims.quote: The call recording setting is now enabled by default to allow for AI-powered lead qualification.
claims.note: The page shows no date. Secondary coverage gives conflicting dates (April 2026 and a July 1, 2026 switch), so verify in an account.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Recording stays off for accounts that had previously turned it off, or whose business is identified as healthcare or financial services.
claims.quote: Call recording will remain turned off if you previously turned it off, or if your business was identified as operating in healthcare or financial services.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Call recording and AI-qualified conversions are limited to calls involving phone numbers in the United States and Canada.
claims.quote: only available for calls involving phone numbers in the United States and Canada

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: A call must go through a Google Forwarding Number, which requires call reporting to be turned on, to be eligible for recording.
claims.quote: Calls must flow through a Google Forwarding Number. This requires call reporting to be turned on in your account settings.

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Calls from website visits are among the call sources eligible for recording.
claims.quote: or calls from website visits are eligible

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Calls from location assets are not supported for recording.
claims.quote: calls from your location assets are not supported for recording at this time

claims.question: Q2
claims.claim: Call recording is automatically skipped for advertisers in sensitive industries, such as specific healthcare or financial services, unless they opt in.
claims.quote: call recording is automatically skipped for advertisers in sensitive industries, like specific healthcare or financial services
claims.note: The page lists healthcare and financial services as examples; legal services are not named.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: On Google Ads recorded calls, the caller hears a short automated message at the start saying the conversation will be recorded for quality purposes.
claims.quote: Callers will hear a short automated message at the beginning of the call notifying them that the conversation will be recorded for quality purposes.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: The caller hears a short message saying the call will be recorded by Google for quality assurance (older Google Ads help wording).
claims.quote: The user will hear a short message informing them that the call will be recorded by Google for quality assurance.

claims.question: Q3
claims.claim: On Local Services Ads, the business hears a "Call from Google" message that identifies the call as coming from the ad.
claims.quote: you’ll hear the message: “Call from Google.”

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: Local Services Ads call recordings and messages are retained up to 180 days in North America before they are destroyed.
claims.quote: Call recordings and messages are retained up to 180 days before they are destroyed.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: Local Services Ads recordings and messages in legal verticals are retained for 60 days, a shorter period than the general 180 days.
claims.quote: Recordings and messages in legal verticals are retained for 60 days.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: Google Ads call recordings are available for playback for 30 days after the call date.
claims.quote: Recorded calls are available for 30 days after the date of the call.

claims.question: Q4
claims.claim: A Local Search Forum reply (Feb 8, 2024) quotes Google's legal-vertical 60-day retention to explain why older LSA calls no longer show.
claims.quote: recordings and messages in legal verticals are retained for 60 days.
claims.note: Forum post by Matt Casady; his role (lawyer, staff, or marketer) is not stated on the page. Quoted policy wording is what matters here.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says Google Ads call recordings are used to evaluate lead quality, monitor spam and fraud, and improve conversion reporting accuracy.
claims.quote: Recordings are used to evaluate lead quality, monitor spam and fraud, and improve the accuracy of your conversion reporting.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says its AI classification of recordings automatically identifies quality leads to improve Smart Bidding.
claims.quote: Automatically identifies quality leads to improve Smart Bidding.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says call recordings let advertisers play back and review conversations inside their reports.
claims.quote: Enables you to play call recordings and review conversations directly within your reports.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google Ads call recordings can be played only in the Google Ads interface and cannot be downloaded.
claims.quote: Call recording is only available using the Google Ads UI and the recordings are not available for download.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says MCC and direct users with Admin or Standard access can play Google Ads call recordings once recording is enabled.
claims.quote: MCC and direct users with Admin or direct users with Standard access will be able to play recordings, once enabled.
claims.note: Google's text does not say who among those users sees the audio beyond playback access.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says information from Google Ads recorded calls is anonymized and used only to detect unauthorized activity and to assess quality in aggregate.
claims.quote: Information taken from calls is anonymized and only used to detect unauthorized activity and assess quality in aggregate.
claims.note: This older page is for call ads and call assets; the current page lists lead-quality and spam uses (see the other Q5 claims).

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says Google Ads call recordings will not be used for ad targeting.
claims.quote: Recordings will not be used for ad targeting purposes.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Local Services Ads providers may review call recordings to track conversations.
claims.quote: Providers may review call recordings in order to track conversations.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says it does not monitor or control how Local Services Ads providers use the recordings they review.
claims.quote: Google does not monitor or control how providers use the recordings.

claims.question: Q5
claims.claim: Google says it reviews Local Services call recordings on a limited basis for purposes such as enforcing policies and monitoring provider experience.
claims.quote: Google reviews emails, texts, or call recordings routed through Google’s system on a limited basis for the following purposes:

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: Turning call recording off stops Google's AI from analyzing Google Ads call conversations for lead quality.
claims.quote: Disabling call recording will prevent the AI from analyzing conversations for lead quality.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: When recording is off, Google Ads falls back to measuring conversions by call duration.
claims.quote: In this case, the system will fall back to using call duration to measure conversions.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: To turn recording on or off, an advertiser opens Admin, then Account settings, then the Call ads drop-down, then sets Call recording to On or Off.
claims.quote: Open the “Call ads” drop-down.
claims.note: The first two steps (Admin menu and Account settings) are described in the page's numbered list; this quote covers the third step.

claims.question: Q6
claims.claim: An advertiser that does not accept the call and messaging ads terms cannot create or edit call ads or call assets.
claims.quote: If you choose not to accept, your account will not be able to create or edit call ads and assets.

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: Local Services Ads says call recordings and messages are not available for health care verticals or tax specialists.
claims.quote: Call recordings and messages aren't available for health care verticals or tax specialists.

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: Google says an advertiser that cannot take part in call recording for legal or regulatory reasons can ask Google for an exemption.
claims.quote: If you have questions about eligibility or can't participate in call recording for legal or regulatory reasons, contact Google to request an exemption from monitoring and recording.

claims.question: Q7
claims.claim: Under the Call Ads Supplemental Terms, HIPAA covered entities and business associates are told to ask Google for exclusion from recording.
claims.quote: to request exclusion from monitoring and recording of Communications

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The North Carolina State Bar Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5, which addressed pay-per-lead ads, at its April 2022 meeting.
claims.quote: Therefore, at its meeting in April 2022, the Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5.
claims.note: Article by Suzanne Lever in the NC State Bar Journal. Status: withdrawn, no final opinion. The article says the Committee is hesitant to opine on specific ad platforms.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The proposed NC opinion was prompted by the platform recording and retaining potential-client communications.
claims.quote: The feature of the advertising program that resulted in the inquiry to the Ethics Committee was the recording and retention of potential client communications by the advertising platform company.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The NC Ethics Committee concluded that the recordings at issue in the pay-per-lead program are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosure.
claims.quote: A review of these thoughtful comments led the Ethics Committee to conclude that the recordings at issue are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosures

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The NC bar reminds lawyers to investigate any advertising program or technology service before participating.
claims.quote: lawyers are reminded of their duty to make reasonable investigations into any advertising program

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The NC article suggests that intake staff tell callers from an ad that the advertising company can record the call and that what they say will not be confidential.
claims.quote: Because you called us by clicking on an advertisement, the advertising company is able to record this call and anything you say will not be confidential.
claims.note: This is wording the article suggests for intake staff, not a rule.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The NC article quotes the Rule 1.18 comment saying a lawyer must warn that a communication will not create a client-lawyer relationship and is not confidential or privileged.
claims.quote: a lawyer has an affirmative obligation to warn the person that a communication with the lawyer will not create a client-lawyer relationship and information conveyed to the lawyer will not be confidential or privileged
claims.note: The article quotes the ABA Model Rule 1.18 comment; it is not a separate NC rule.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: Connecticut Bar Informal Opinion 2013-08 (June 19, 2013) assumes callers are warned before any call recording.
claims.quote: This opinion is based on the understanding that all callers will be notified prior to any recording.
claims.note: Not Google-specific: it concerns a Yellow Pages pay-per-call service. Informal opinion from 2013; I found no later Connecticut opinion on this point.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: Connecticut Informal Opinion 2013-08 requires the vendor contract to deny the pay-per-call vendor access to recordings.
claims.quote: the contract must provide that Yellow Pages will not have access to the recordings
claims.note: Not Google-specific; analogous pay-per-call vendor case. A warning alone was not treated as enough.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: Connecticut Informal Opinion 2013-08 says lawyers must avoid communication methods that pose an unreasonable risk of inadvertent disclosure, including for potential clients.
claims.quote: the duty of confidentiality established by Rules 1.6 and 1.18 requires a lawyer to avoid using a means of communication with clients or potential clients that poses an unreasonable risk of inadvertent disclosure to third parties.
claims.note: Not Google-specific; applies Rules 1.6 and 1.18 to a pay-per-call recording vendor.

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: Under the Call Ads Supplemental Terms, the advertiser confirms it has given notice to its agents, employees and other participants that calls may be monitored or recorded by Google.
claims.quote: You have provided notice to your agents, employees, and any other party that may participate in the Communications that (a) these Communications may be monitored or recorded by Google

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: Under the Call Ads Supplemental Terms, the advertiser confirms it has obtained the express consent of its agents, employees and other participants to monitoring, recording and use.
claims.quote: and you have obtained their express consent to such monitoring and recording and use

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: The Call Ads Supplemental Terms say Google may monitor and record a sample of calls, texts, live chats and other communications started through the advertising programs.
claims.quote: Google may monitor and record a sample of telephone calls, text messages, live chat, and other communications initiated through the Programs

claims.question: Q10
claims.claim: Under the Call Ads Supplemental Terms, the advertiser and other participants must comply with the TCPA and other applicable laws when using the communication features.
claims.quote: You and any other party that may participate in the Communications will comply with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and other applicable laws when using the Communication Features

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: NYC Bar Formal Opinion 2026-2 on recording prospective-client calls with AI tools; a secondary summary (Ezel) only. Not Google-specific.
leads.why_not_a_claim: I read only a secondary summary, not the City Bar's own opinion, and it concerns AI recording tools rather than Google ads.

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: Orange County Bar Association 'Ethically Speaking' column (Dec 2021) on recording initial client calls as a marketing mishap.
leads.why_not_a_claim: The page returned no content when fetched (blocked or empty).

leads.question: Q8
leads.what: Full text of the NC State Bar's Proposed 2021 FEO 5 (pay-per-lead advertising), as covered by a 2021 news article.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Not opened; I relied on the NC Bar's 2022 article for the withdrawal and rationale.

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Reddit search for Google Ads or LSA call recording threads on r/LawFirm (the subreddit search endpoint).
leads.why_not_a_claim: Reddit returned a login page instead of results, and the search tool blocks reddit.com; no Reddit thread was read.

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Local Search Forum thread on Google Local Services Ads dispute denials (2021), where a poster mentions recordings of calls they should not have been charged for.
leads.why_not_a_claim: The poster does not say they are a lawyer, staff member or marketer for a firm; the thread is about disputes and charges, not about Google recording calls.

leads.question: Q9
leads.what: Local Search Forum reply by Matt Casady (Feb 8, 2024) citing Google's 60-day legal-vertical retention; it is captured as a Q4 claim.
leads.why_not_a_claim: His role (lawyer, staff or marketer) is not stated on the page, so it is not logged as a Q9 first-hand statement.

leads.question: Q10
leads.what: Law-marketing blog (LaFleur) on the 2025 Local Services Ads terms and attorney-client privilege, quoting older LSA terms that require advertisers to notify staff.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Secondary vendor commentary; I saw only search excerpts, not the full page, and it is not Google's current LSA terms.

leads.question: Q10
leads.what: Reclaim The Net article on Google's updated Local Services Ads terms and confidentiality in medical and legal sectors.
leads.why_not_a_claim: Secondary commentary; not opened, and Google's primary LSA terms text was not located.
